title: Reported “Freedom Drive” convoy from Riga toward Daugavpils
location: Reported Riga-to-Daugavpils route; Grani and Latgales Laiks place police intervention under Jēkabpils and a Daugavpils gathering at a fuel station on Stacijas Street; blocked Pietiek preview mentioned Rumbula.
scope: One reported cross-city convoy on Jan. 9 within a recurring Freedom Drive campaign. Exact route, whether route participants and the Daugavpils fuel-station gathering form one coding unit, and any separate local action remain under review. Earlier December drives are separate dated actions; no continuous episode is inferred.
organizer: Association Sabiedriskie Satversmes Sargi; LZ identifies Jānis Pļaviņš and Arnolds Babris among organizers/participants in a livestream.
participants_original: No numerical person estimate. Sources say only part of the convoy reached Daugavpils; no vehicle count is converted into persons. Newspaper photo is not counted.
threshold_50_evidence: No source verifies 50 concurrent public participants. Person count, vehicle occupancy and any local assembly size remain unknown; eligibility is pending the 50-person threshold.

occurrence.summary: Opened contemporaneous LZ, Grani and Latgales Laiks reporting support a Jan. 9 drive from Riga toward Daugavpils and a gathering among those who reached the city.

start_date.summary: LZ says a Jan. 8 invitation was for the preceding Saturday, and Jan. 11–12 reporting describes the preceding drive. Latgales Laiks page-1 lede visibly prints “9 December”; retain conflict in G011.

location.summary: Opened Grani and Latgales Laiks place police intervention under Jēkabpils and identify the Stacijas Street fuel-station gathering. Pietiek.info returned HTTP403; its search preview mentioned Rumbula and is not verified body evidence.

organizer.summary: LZ identifies association Sabiedriskie Satversmes Sargi and says its livestream showed Jānis Pļaviņš and Arnolds Babris among organizers/participants; retain that attribution without assigning more specific roles.

demands.summary: Opened reports characterize the drive as opposition to COVID restrictions, compulsory vaccination and masks for schoolchildren. Funeral-procession symbolism about Viņķele alone does not establish a separate demand to remove the minister.

end_date.summary: Latgales Laiks describes a same-day Daugavpils gathering followed by the participants returning after police protocols and verbal exchange. Jan. 9 is used as the bounded action date; the printed “9 December” conflict remains in G011.

participants.summary: No numeric headcount or concurrent size. Vehicles, the “only part” reaching Daugavpils, and a photograph do not establish a 50-person crowd.

protester_violence.summary: LZ attributes aggression and repeated disobedience to some people in the police account, but does not report physical violence; Latgales Laiks describes a loud verbal exchange. Physical violence remains unknown.

state_response.summary: LZ says some people were taken to a station for clarification after identity concealment/repeated disobedience (number unknown), supporting arrests=yes with attribution. Grani and Latgales Laiks report police stopped cars and barred some from continuing, supporting crowd_dispersal=yes as an attempt to impede the convoy; no force is inferred. No evidence found for other response categories.

notes: Physical event evidence is now opened, but 50 concurrent people are unverified. Latgales Laiks issue dated Jan. 12 has page-1 lede printed “9 December”; Jan. 9 is supported by LZ invitation context and Jan. 11–12 coverage, with conflict retained. Grani and Latgales Laiks report police stopped cars and barred some from continuing, supporting an attempt to impede the convoy; no force inferred. LZ says some people were taken to a station after identity concealment/repeated disobedience; count unknown. Its Babris defamation case is separate from protest arrests. Route, participant threshold and episode unit remain unresolved. Dec. 12/19/26 actions are separate dated drives, not automatic continuations.
open_questions: Can any source establish 50 concurrent actual persons in the convoy or Daugavpils gathering?
Does the coding unit include the convoy route and destination fuel-station assembly together, or distinct actions?
Can the conflicting printed “9 December” date be independently explained without silently correcting the newspaper?
Can police action be attributed to impeding a public assembly specifically, rather than stopping vehicles along the route?
Is any separate Latvia-directed demand to remove the health minister evidenced beyond the restriction-related demands?
